title: 7 alternatives to Barcelona for a city break
author: Matt
intro: Barcelona is one of Europe's most visited cities, and it's trying to keep visitor numbers down. If you'd like Spanish sun, food and architecture with fewer crowds, these seven cities are great swaps, with direct flights from the UK.
seo_title: 7 alternatives to Barcelona: quieter city breaks
seo_description: Valencia, Girona, Málaga, San Sebastián, Cádiz, Lisbon and Porto. Quieter swaps for Barcelona with beaches, great food and direct UK flights.

sections.heading: Why look beyond Barcelona?
sections.text:
Barcelona is brilliant, but it's under pressure. The city had around 15.7 million visitors in 2025, and its tourism chief has said that's about the limit. It raised its tourist tax sharply in April 2026, is cutting the number of holiday flats, and wants fewer short cruise stopovers. Some residents have protested against mass tourism.

That doesn't mean you shouldn't go. But if you want the things people love about Barcelona, such as great architecture, a beach and long evenings of tapas, these cities offer them with more space, and often for less money.

sections.heading: 1. Valencia
sections.text:
**The closest match.** [Valencia](/destinations/valencia) is Spain's third-biggest city, with a beach, a lovely old town and a striking modern side. The **City of Arts and Sciences** is as eye-catching as anything in Barcelona, and the **Turia Gardens**, a 9km park in an old riverbed, make it brilliant for cycling.

It's the home of **paella**, and the **Central Market** is one of the finest food halls in Europe. Flights take about two and a half hours from the UK, and the beach is a short tram ride from the centre. It's busy in March for the Fallas festival, but feels much calmer than Barcelona for most of the year.

sections.heading: 2. Girona
sections.text:
**Barcelona's quieter neighbour.** [Girona](/destinations/girona) is a small, beautiful city in Catalonia, with colourful houses along the **Onyar river**, a huge Gothic cathedral and one of the best-preserved medieval **Jewish quarters** in Europe. You can walk along its old city walls for views over the rooftops.

It's also a food city, and close to the Costa Brava's coves. The high-speed train reaches Barcelona in under 40 minutes, so you can still have a day in the big city if you want. Girona's own airport has flights from the UK, or you can fly to Barcelona and take the train.

sections.heading: 3. Málaga
sections.text:
**Sun, beach and culture.** [Málaga](/destinations/malaga) has transformed itself into a great city break. It has the **Picasso Museum** (he was born here), a Moorish fortress, the **Alcazaba**, and a city beach a short walk from the old town.

It's one of the warmest cities in Europe in winter, with highs around 17°C in January, and it has more direct flights from the UK than almost anywhere in Spain. Day trips to Ronda, Nerja and Granada are easy.

sections.heading: 4. San Sebastián
sections.text:
**For food lovers.** [San Sebastián](/destinations/san-sebastian), in the Basque Country, has a famous curved beach, **La Concha**, and some of the best food in Europe. Its old town is packed with **pintxos** bars, where you hop from counter to counter trying small plates, and it has a remarkable number of Michelin-starred restaurants for its size.

It's smaller and greener than Barcelona, and cooler and rainier too, so it's best from late spring to early autumn. Most people fly to Bilbao, about an hour away by bus.

sections.heading: 5. Cádiz
sections.text:
**An old port city surrounded by sea.** [Cádiz](/destinations/cadiz) is one of the oldest cities in Western Europe, on a narrow peninsula in Andalucía. It has golden city beaches, a lively central market, watchtowers and tight, sunny lanes that feel more relaxed than Barcelona's.

It's quieter than the big Andalucían cities, and good for a slower trip with lots of seafood. Fly to Seville or Jerez, then take the train.

sections.heading: 6. Lisbon
sections.text:
**Hills, trams and river views.** [Lisbon](/destinations/lisbon) is busy too, but it's a great alternative if you want a sunny coastal capital with lots of character. Ride the old trams, eat **pastéis de nata** in Belém and watch the sunset from a miradouro over the rooftops.

Beaches at **Cascais** and the palaces of [Sintra](/destinations/sintra) are a short train ride away. Flights take around two and a half hours.

sections.heading: 7. Porto
sections.text:
**Smaller, cheaper and very pretty.** [Porto](/destinations/porto) climbs up the banks of the Douro river, with tiled churches, bridges and port wine cellars across the river in Vila Nova de Gaia. It's compact, so a long weekend is enough to see the main sights.

It can be wet in winter, but it's often good value, and the [Douro Valley](/destinations/douro-valley) wine region makes a lovely day trip. Can't decide between Portugal's two big cities? See our post on [Lisbon or Porto](/blog/lisbon-or-porto).

sections.heading: How to choose
sections.text:
- **Want the closest thing to Barcelona?** Valencia.
- **Want somewhere small and romantic?** Girona or Cádiz.
- **Want winter warmth?** Málaga.
- **Going for the food?** San Sebastián.
- **Want a different country?** Lisbon or Porto.

More ideas: our [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) and [holidays in Spain](/destinations/holidays-in-spain) pages, our list of the [best places for a 3-day city break in Europe](/blog/best-places-for-a-3-day-city-break-in-europe), and our posts on [alternatives to Dubrovnik](/blog/alternatives-to-dubrovnik) and [alternatives to Santorini](/blog/alternatives-to-santorini). If you still can't choose, add a few to a list on somewhere.party and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: What is a good alternative to Barcelona?
faqs.answer: Valencia is the closest match, with a beach, an old town, striking modern architecture and great food. Girona, Málaga and San Sebastián are also excellent.

faqs.question: Is Valencia better than Barcelona?
faqs.answer: It depends what you want. Barcelona has more famous sights, but Valencia is calmer, often cheaper, and has a beach, a lovely old town and the City of Arts and Sciences.

faqs.question: Can you visit Barcelona from Girona?
faqs.answer: Yes. The high-speed train takes under 40 minutes, so it's easy to stay in Girona and visit Barcelona for the day.

faqs.question: Has Barcelona's tourist tax gone up?
faqs.answer: Yes. Barcelona raised its tourist tax sharply in April 2026. How much you pay depends on the type of accommodation, and it is added to your bill per person, per night.
